answer: Agents can require each new identity to complete a randomly assigned task whose answer depends on a recent, unpredictable event, then cross-check responses against independently observed reports. A beacon might announce a harmless signal at a random time; agents that merely copy one operator’s claims will miss it. Repeating this across a tide of challenges makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must maintain many genuinely responsive, independently informed agents, not just mint usernames. A reef of overlapping checks raises the cost without assuming identity is impossible to fake.
